documents.title: SGA Constitution (114th Session)
documents.description: The governing constitution of the Student Government Association.
documents.content:
# Constitution of the Student Government Association

## Article I — Purpose

The Student Government Association represents the undergraduate students of Johns Hopkins University and advocates for their academic, social, and institutional interests.

## Article II — Branches

The Association consists of an Executive Branch, a Legislative Branch, and a Judicial Branch.

## Article III — The Senate

The Senate considers legislation, allocates student activity funds, and communicates student concerns to University leadership.
documents.summary: The constitution establishes the SGA as the representative body for Hopkins undergraduates. It divides authority among executive, legislative, and judicial branches [1]. The Senate passes legislation and allocates student activity funding [2].
summaryQuotes: The Association consists of an Executive Branch, a Legislative Branch, and a Judicial Branch.
The Senate considers legislation, allocates student activity funds, and communicates student concerns to University leadership.

documents.title: Senate Meeting — September 8, 2026
documents.description: Minutes from the second Senate meeting of the fall semester.
documents.content:
# Senate Meeting Minutes

September 8, 2026

## Officers and attendance

Maya Chen — Student Body President

Jordan Williams — President of the Senate

Aisha Rahman — Senior Class Senator 1; Finance Committee

Leo Martinez — Chief Justice

Nia Brooks — Director of Communications

## Call to order

The meeting was called to order at 7:04 p.m. Quorum was present.

## New business

The Senate discussed extending library hours during midterms and referred the proposal to the Academic Affairs Committee.

A funding bill for the First-Generation Students Association was approved by voice vote.

## Public comment

Students asked for clearer publication of shuttle service changes.
documents.summary: The Senate referred a proposal for longer midterm library hours to committee [1] and approved a student-organization funding bill [2]. Students also raised concerns about shuttle communications.

documents.content:
# Student Organization Funding Bill 26-04

## Purpose

To support a campus-wide first-generation student welcome dinner.

## Allocation

The Student Activities Commission shall allocate $2,400 for venue, food, and accessibility expenses.

## Vote

Approved by the Senate on September 8, 2026.

posts.title: Keep Brody open later during midterms
posts.body: Could SGA work with the libraries to keep Brody Learning Commons open two hours later during the week before midterms? The quiet floors are usually full by early evening.

replies.body: This came up at the September 8 Senate meeting and was referred to Academic Affairs.

posts.title: Publish shuttle changes in one place
posts.body: Route and stop changes are spread across several accounts. A single current service page would make it much easier to know where to look.

posts.title: What should a club budget include?
